newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian senator says to sell bank shares.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian senator says to sell bank shares.

text.p: Australian senator Brian Gibson, who is parliamentary secretary to Treasurer Peter Costello, has revealed he will dispose of shares in the National Australia Bank Ltd and the Bank of Melbourne Ltd.

"I have ... given instructions to my broker for the immediate sale of all shares owned jointly by my wife and myself in both the National Australia Bank Ltd and Bank of Melbourne Ltd," Gibson said in a statement.
Gibson, a senator from the state of Tasmania, announced the sale late on Sunday as controversy over government ministers' equity investments flared up.

Assistant treasurer Jim Short resigned on Sunday after it was revealed his shares in Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd may have placed him in breach of Prime Minister John Howard's ministerial guidelines.
Under the guidelines, ministers are required to divest themselves of all shares and similar interests in any company or business involved in the area of their portfolio.
Gibson said he believed he had not breached the guidelines as he had no direct portfolio responsibility for banking.

"Nevertheless, following the matters raised against Senator Jim Short and in order to ensure that there can be no misrepresentation to the community, my wife and I have decided to take this action," he said.
Controvery also arose over the weekend regarding Tanya Costello's shares in Commonwealth Bank of Australia.
However, Howard said on Monday Costello had not breached the guidelines by allowing his wife to hold the shares.
